iis.name: Immunization Information Systems (IIS) monthly submissions to CDC
iis.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
iis.location: Monthly Cumulative Number and Percent of Persons Who Received Influenza and RSV Immunizations by Jurisdiction (FluVaxView and RSVVaxView dashboards)
iis.description: Immunization Information Systems (IIS) are the confidential, population-based registries that states, some large cities, and territories use to record vaccine doses given by participating providers. Jurisdictions submit aggregate counts to CDC each month, by age group, of residents with at least one dose of seasonal influenza vaccine (children 6 months-17 years and adults 18 and older, 2022-23 season onward), RSV vaccine (adults 75 and older, 2024-25 onward), and RSV monoclonal antibody (infants under 8 months, 2024-25 onward). Counts are cumulative from the start of the season and are divided by the previous year's Census population estimate to give coverage. Because a registry is meant to capture every dose rather than a sample, no standard errors are published. Completeness varies with each jurisdiction's reporting laws and provider participation, so IIS coverage usually runs below survey estimates from the National Immunization Survey. Not all jurisdictions report: 54 submitted data through the 2024-25 season and about half did in 2025-26, and CDC does not publish a national estimate. New York City and Philadelphia report separately from their states; Chicago and Houston have reported separately in some seasons.
iis.restrictions: Public domain. CDC data is generally not subject to copyright restrictions.
